properties.decision:
reflow2 will not tell you a test is hollow. It cannot read an assertion and see that it says `true === true`, cannot see that mocking has hollowed the execution path out, and cannot see an exception swallowed inside a test that then exits zero. A Verification marked `passing` is a CLAIM SOMEBODY MADE, and reflow2 records it, counts it toward coverage, and reports it as passing.

WHOSE JOB IT IS: a mutation-testing tool, a coverage tool that measures real paths, and a reviewer who runs the check with the code deliberately broken.

⚠️ WHY IT IS WRITTEN DOWN, and this one is the most load-bearing of the four. Verification coverage is one of reflow2's headline numbers — "123 of 162 capabilities verified" appears in its own report. THAT NUMBER COUNTS CHECKS, NOT CONFIDENCE. A design can reach 100% verified on tests that could not fail, and reflow2 would report full coverage and be correct about what it measured. Anthony named tautological testing, excessive mocking and swallowed exceptions as a pitfall class on 2026-08-17; none of the three is visible from here.

⭐ AND REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY BEEN BITTEN BY IT, which is why this is evidenced rather than theoretical. `ver:search-first-forces-a-choice` records: "A FOURTH MUTATION EXPOSED A VACUOUS TEST OF MY OWN ... the first revision test passed whether or not the guard was there, because a revision with no near neighbour has nothing to report either way." A hollow test inside reflow2's own suite, found by mutating the code — not by anything reflow2 computed. Its status said `passing` throughout, truthfully.

⇒ WHAT REFLOW2 DOES DO NEARBY: it distinguishes a check that PASSES from one that merely EXISTS (a `planned` check does not silence `unverified_capability`), it reports when a check last ran and flags a stale-but-passing one, and it refuses to treat component-granularity coverage as capability coverage. So it polices the BOOKKEEPING around checks rigorously and the CONTENT of them not at all.

📌 THE ADJACENT WORK, and it is the reachable half rather than a contradiction of this non-goal: reflow2 could record whether a check was PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL — mutation-checked — because that is a fact an author can state and a reader can rely on. It cannot judge the check; it can carry the claim. That is a candidate use of the evidence field `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` asks for. This non-goal covers the judging, not the recording.

RECORDED AS A NON-GOAL, 2026-08-17. Retiring it is part of shipping anything that voids it.
properties.name: NON-GOAL — reflow2 does not judge whether a check is MEANINGFUL; a passing Verification is a claim it records, never one it validates
properties.rationale: Verification coverage is a headline reflow2 number and it counts checks, not confidence — a design can reach 100% verified on tests that could not fail. Evidenced rather than theoretical: reflow2's own suite carried a hollow test that reported passing truthfully throughout, found by mutating code rather than by anything reflow2 computed. It polices the bookkeeping around checks rigorously and their content not at all.
